claim: Acid sphingomyelinase (Asm) hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide.
source: Asm hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide, which is further metabolized to sphingosine by Ac.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established biochemical fact about Asm function.

claim: Ceramide is further metabolized to sphingosine by acid ceramidase (Ac).
source: Asm hydrolyzes sphingomyelin to ceramide, which is further metabolized to sphingosine by Ac.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as an established biochemical fact about Ac function.

claim: Ceramide generates ceramide-enriched platforms that are involved in receptor clustering within cellular membranes.
source: Ceramide generates ceramide-enriched platforms that are involved in receptor clustering within cellular membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citation in the introduction.

claim: T cell-specific ablation of Asm in Smpd1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Asm/CD4cre) mice resulted in enhanced tumor progression.
source: T cell-specific ablation of Asm in Smpd1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Asm/CD4cre) mice resulted in enhanced tumor progression associated with impaired T cell responses
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4A.

claim: T cell-specific ablation of Asm in Asm/CD4cre mice resulted in impaired T cell responses.
source: T cell-specific ablation of Asm in Smpd1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Asm/CD4cre) mice resulted in enhanced tumor progression associated with impaired T cell responses
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Asah1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Ac/CD4cre) mice showed reduced tumor growth rates compared to controls upon tumor transplantation.
source: whereas Asah1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Ac/CD4cre) mice showed reduced tumor growth rates and elevated T cell activation compared to the respective controls upon tumor transplantation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 8A.

claim: Ac/CD4cre mice showed elevated T cell activation compared to controls upon tumor transplantation.
source: whereas Asah1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Ac/CD4cre) mice showed reduced tumor growth rates and elevated T cell activation compared to the respective controls upon tumor transplantation.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 8C.

claim: Decreased ceramide content supports CD4+ regulatory T cell differentiation.
source: Further in vitro analysis revealed that decreased ceramide content supports CD4+ regulatory T cell differentiation and interferes with cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro experimental data in Figures 1E and 3.

claim: Decreased ceramide content interferes with cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells.
source: Further in vitro analysis revealed that decreased ceramide content supports CD4+ regulatory T cell differentiation and interferes with cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro experimental data in Figure 3D.

claim: Elevated ceramide concentration in CD8+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice was associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity.
source: In contrast, elevated ceramide concentration in CD8+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice was associated with enhanced cytotoxic activity.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6F.

claim: Ceramide co-localized with the T cell receptor (TCR) in the membrane of stimulated T cells.
source: Strikingly, ceramide co-localized with the T cell receptor (TCR) and CD3 in the membrane of stimulated T cells
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by microscopy data in Figure 5.

claim: Ceramide co-localized with CD3 in the membrane of stimulated T cells.
source: Strikingly, ceramide co-localized with the T cell receptor (TCR) and CD3 in the membrane of stimulated T cells
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by microscopy data in Figure 5A.

claim: Phosphorylation of TCR signaling molecules was elevated in Ac-deficient T cells.
source: and phosphorylation of TCR signaling molecules was elevated in Ac-deficient T cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figure 6C and 6D.

claim: Ceramide has the ability to form ceramide-enriched platforms within the plasma membrane.
source: Ceramide has the ability to form ceramide-enriched platforms within the plasma membrane (Kolesnick et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Ceramide-enriched microdomains contribute to receptor clustering and other protein interactions.
source: These microdomains contribute to receptor clustering and other protein interactions and are thereby involved in several signaling pathways and important cellular processes including proliferation, migration, differentiation, and apoptosis (Zhang et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Mutations in the SMPD1 gene resulting in loss of or reduced Asm activity cause Niemann-Pick type A and B disease.
source: Specifically, mutations in the SMPD1 gene, encoding for Asm, resulting in loss of or reduced Asm activity, cause the lipid-storage disease Niemann-Pick type A and B (NPD) (Schuchman and Wasserstein, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: NPD type A patients suffer from severe neuronal symptoms due to sphingomyelin accumulations in the central nervous system.
source: NPD type A patients suffer from severe neuronal symptoms, due to sphingomyelin accumulations in the central nervous system (Ohno, 1995).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Elevated Asm activity is associated with the development of major depressive disorders.
source: In contrast, elevated Asm activity is associated with the development of major depressive disorders (Kornhuber et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Pharmacological inhibitors of Asm (FIASMA) are used as antidepressant drugs.
source: Pharmacological inhibitors of Asm (functional inhibitors of Asm, FIASMA) are therefore used as antidepressant drugs (Beckmann et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of Ac activity leads to the development of Farber disease.
source: Loss of Ac activity leads to the development of Farber disease (FD).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established medical knowledge.

claim: FD patients suffer from arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly, and a general developmental delay.
source: FD patients suffer from arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly, and a general developmental delay (Yu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Asm-generated ceramide-enriched platforms are crucial for the CD95-mediated induction of apoptosis.
source: For instance, Asm-generated ceramide-enriched platforms are crucial for the CD95-mediated induction of apoptosis (Grassmé et al., 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Cancer cells may upregulate Ac expression, leading to reduced ceramide abundance and increased levels of pro-survival lipid sphingosine-1-phosphate (S-1-P).
source: Cancer cells may upregulate Ac expression, leading to reduced ceramide abundance and increased levels of pro-survival lipid sphingosine-1-phosphate (S-1-P) and thereby foster their survival (Morad and Cabot, 2013; Baran et al., 2007; Flowers et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Ionizing radiation induces the activity of Asm, leading to ceramide generation and apoptosis of cancer cells.
source: For example, ionizing radiation induces the activity of Asm, leading to ceramide generation and apoptosis of cancer cells, but fails to do so in lymphoblasts from NPD patients, which lack Asm activity (Santana et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Ionizing radiation fails to induce apoptosis in lymphoblasts from NPD patients, which lack Asm activity.
source: For example, ionizing radiation induces the activity of Asm, leading to ceramide generation and apoptosis of cancer cells, but fails to do so in lymphoblasts from NPD patients, which lack Asm activity (Santana et al., 1996).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: There was an elevated incidence for cancer in NPD patients.
source: In addition, Mauhin et al., 2021 demonstrated most recently, in a retrospective study, that there was an elevated incidence for cancer in NPD patients.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Enhanced tumor growth rate of transplanted tumor cells was observed in Asm-deficient mice compared to wildtype mice.
source: We previously observed an enhanced tumor growth rate of transplanted tumor cells in Asm-deficient mice as compared to wildtype (WT) mice.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a previous finding by the authors.

claim: Apoptosis-resistant endothelial cells in Asm-deficient mice were identified as a driver of elevated tumor growth.
source: Investigation of the tumor microvasculature identified apoptosis-resistant endothelial cells in Asm-deficient mice as a driver of elevated tumor growth (Garcia-Barros, 2003).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Ac facilitates proliferation of various cancer cell lines by the degradation of ceramide.
source: In various cancer cell lines, Ac facilitates proliferation by the degradation of ceramide (Govindarajah et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Pharmacological inhibition of Ac has been described to be effective for the treatment of patients suffering from colorectal cancer.
source: Pharmacological inhibition of Ac has been described to be effective for the treatment of patients suffering from colorectal cancer (Sakamoto et al., 2005).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Application of exogenous C2 ceramide induces a strong anti-tumor response by increasing frequencies of cytotoxic CD8+ and IFN-γ-producing CD4+ T cells.
source: Emphasizing the important role of ceramide in the modulation of tumorigenesis, recent studies by Ghosh et al. provided evidence that the application of exogenous C2 ceramide induces a strong anti-tumor response by increasing frequencies of cytotoxic CD8+ and IFN-γ-producing CD4+ T cells (Ghosh et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: The ratio of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells versus CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells in the tumor microenvironment is predictive for the disease outcome in melanoma patients.
source: In melanoma patients, the ratio of cytotoxic CD8+ T cells versus CD4+Foxp3+ regulatory T cells (Tregs) in the tumor microenvironment is predictive for the disease outcome (Jacobs et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Neuropilin-1 is highly expressed by Tregs.
source: We provided evidence that Neuropilin-1, highly expressed by Tregs (Bruder et al., 2004), regulates the migration of Tregs into VEGF-producing tumor tissue accompanied by elevated tumor progression (Hansen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Neuropilin-1 regulates the migration of Tregs into VEGF-producing tumor tissue accompanied by elevated tumor progression.
source: We provided evidence that Neuropilin-1, highly expressed by Tregs (Bruder et al., 2004), regulates the migration of Tregs into VEGF-producing tumor tissue accompanied by elevated tumor progression (Hansen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Depletion of Tregs improved the anti-tumoral immune response of CD8+ T cells in colitis-associated colon cancer.
source: Depletion of Tregs improved the anti-tumoral immune response of CD8+ T cells in colitis-associated colon cancer, emphasizing the important role of the T cell composition in tumorigenesis (Pastille et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Asm-deficient mice showed an impaired cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells during LCMV infection.
source: Analysis of immune responses in Asm-deficient mice has shown an impaired cytotoxic activity of CD8+ T cells during LCMV infection (Herz et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Asm has been identified as a negative regulator of Treg development.
source: Moreover, Asm has been identified as a negative regulator of Treg development (Zhou et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Asm-deficient or FIASMA-treated mice showed increased numbers of Tregs in comparison to WT animals.
source: Asm-deficient or FIASMA-treated mice showed increased numbers of Tregs in comparison to WT animals (Hollmann et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Lower Treg frequencies were detected in spleens of t-Asm/CD4cre mice, which overexpress Asm specifically in T cells.
source: In accordance, we detected lower Treg frequencies in spleens of t-Asm/CD4cre mice, which overexpress Asm specifically in T cells (Hose et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation to the authors' previous work.

claim: Inhibition of Asm in CD4+ T cells isolated from human peripheral blood led to impaired T cell receptor signal transduction.
source: In CD4+ T cells, isolated from human peripheral blood, inhibition of Asm led to an impaired T cell receptor (TCR) signal transduction accompanied by reduced T cell proliferation and impaired CD4+ T helper (Th) cell differentiation (Bai et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Inhibition of Asm in CD4+ T cells isolated from human peripheral blood led to reduced T cell proliferation.
source: In CD4+ T cells, isolated from human peripheral blood, inhibition of Asm led to an impaired T cell receptor (TCR) signal transduction accompanied by reduced T cell proliferation and impaired CD4+ T helper (Th) cell differentiation (Bai et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Inhibition of Asm in CD4+ T cells isolated from human peripheral blood led to impaired CD4+ T helper cell differentiation.
source: In CD4+ T cells, isolated from human peripheral blood, inhibition of Asm led to an impaired T cell receptor (TCR) signal transduction accompanied by reduced T cell proliferation and impaired CD4+ T helper (Th) cell differentiation (Bai et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Asm-deficient mice show significantly accelerated tumor growth rates compared to WT mice.
source: We observed significantly accelerated tumor growth rates in Asm-deficient mice compared to WT mice as previously described (Garcia-Barros, 2003; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and a citation.

claim: Lower frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells were detected in dLNs of tumor bearing Asm-deficient mice compared to WT mice.
source: We detected lower frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in dLNs but increased frequencies of Tregs in tumor bearing Asm-deficient mice compared to WT mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Increased frequencies of Tregs were detected in tumors of Asm-deficient mice compared to WT mice.
source: We detected lower frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in dLNs but increased frequencies of Tregs in tumor bearing Asm-deficient mice compared to WT mice (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: CD4+ and CD8+ TILs from Asm-deficient mice showed reduced expression of IFN-γ and CD44.
source: Furthermore, CD4+ and CD8+ TILs showed a reduced expression of IFN-γ and CD44 (Figure 1C), indicating a decreased T cell response in Asm-deficient mice during tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Enhanced tumor growth in Asm-deficient mice correlates with an insufficient T cell response.
source: These results suggest that elevated tumor growth in Asm-deficient mice correlates with an insufficient T cell response.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented in Figure 1.

claim: Enhanced tumor progression was detected in amitriptyline-treated mice compared to tumor-bearing mice that received the vehicle.
source: Indeed, we detected enhanced tumor progression in amitriptyline-treated mice compared to tumor-bearing mice that received the vehicle.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Amitriptyline-treated C57BL/6 mice showed reduced activation of TILs in terms of IFN-γ and CD44 expression compared to PBS-treated mice.
source: This was accompanied by reduced activation of TILs in terms of IFN-γ and CD44 expression in amitriptyline-treated C57BL/6 mice compared to PBS-treated mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A, B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Elevated Treg frequencies were detected in spleens of naïve Asm-KO mice compared to controls.
source: In accordance with results from Hollmann et al., 2016 and our own study of Asm-overexpressing T cells (Hose et al., 2019), we detected elevated Treg frequencies in spleens of naïve Asm-KO mice as compared to controls (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1D and citations.

claim: CD4+CD25− T cells from Asm-KO mice showed an improved capacity to differentiate into Tregs in vitro when Asm activity is absent.
source: Moreover, induction of Tregs in vitro revealed an improved capacity of CD4+CD25− T cells to differentiate into Tregs when Asm activity is absent (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: T cell-intrinsic Asm activity regulates T cell function and differentiation via the generation of ceramide.
source: These results indicate that the T cell-intrinsic Asm activity regulates T cell function and differentiation most likely via the generation of ceramide.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented in the study.

claim: Tumors of CD4+ T cell-depleted Asm-deficient mice showed higher tumor growth rates than CD4+ T cell-depleted Asm-WT mice.
source: Still, tumors of CD4+ T cell-depleted Asm-deficient mice showed higher tumor growth rates than CD4+ T cell-depleted Asm-WT mice (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by tumor growth data in Figure 2A.

claim: Depletion of CD4+ T cells in Asm-WT mice abolished tumor progression almost completely.
source: Remarkably, depletion of CD4+ T cells in Asm-WT mice abolished tumor progression almost completely.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by tumor growth data in Figure 2A.

claim: CD8+ TILs from Asm-deficient mice revealed reduced expression of IFN-γ, CD44, and granzyme B compared to Asm-WT mice after CD4+ T cell depletion.
source: Strikingly, analysis of CD8+ TILs from Asm-deficient mice revealed reduced expression of activation-associated molecules like IFN-γ, CD44, and granzyme B as compared to Asm-WT mice after CD4+ T cell depletion (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Asm-deficiency interferes with CD8+ T cell responses in tumor-bearing mice independent of CD4+ T cells.
source: These results indicate that Asm-deficiency interferes with CD8+ T cell responses in tumor-bearing mice independent of CD4+ T cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the CD4+ T cell depletion experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Asm/CD4cre mice lack Asm expression specifically in T cells.
source: To exclude an impact of other Asm-deficient cells present in Asm-KO mice, we made use of Smpd1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ (Asm/CD4cre) mice, which lack Asm expression specifically in T cells (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice have significantly reduced ceramide levels compared to T cells from WT littermates.
source: This results in significantly reduced ceramide levels in unstimulated, as well as anti-CD3/anti-CD28 stimulated CD8+ and CD4+ T cells compared to T cells from WT littermates (Smpd1fl/fl/Cd4+/+) (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In vitro stimulation of sorted CD8+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice led to reduced expression of CD25, CD69, and CD44 compared to Asm-proficient CD8+ T cells after 24 hr of stimulation.
source: Consistent with decreased T cell activation observed in tumor-bearing Asm-KO mice, in vitro stimulation of sorted CD8+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice led to reduced expression of early T cell activation-associated molecules. This was reflected by lower CD25, CD69, and CD44 expression among Asm-deficient CD8+ T cells compared to Asm-proficient CD8+ T cells after 24 hr of stimulation (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Antigen-specific CTLs from Asm/CD4cre/OT-I mice showed a reduced killing capacity compared to controls.
source: Moreover, co-cultivation of antigen-specific cytotoxic lymphocytes (CTLs), generated from Asm/CD4cre/OT-I mice, together with ovalbumin(OVA)-loaded target cells revealed a reduced killing capacity of Asm-deficient CD8+ T cells (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by killing assay data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: CD8+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice showed reduced granzyme B expression in response to TCR stimulation.
source: Well in line, CD8+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice showed reduced granzyme B expression in response to TCR stimulation (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The reduced granzyme B expression phenotype in Asm-deficient CD8+ T cells was partially rescued by the addition of exogenous C16 ceramide during stimulation.
source: Strikingly, this phenotype was partially rescued by the addition of exogenous C16 ceramide during stimulation (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Ceramide is important for effective CD8+ T cell responses in vitro.
source: Altogether, these data indicate that ceramide is important for effective CD8+ T cell responses, at least in vitro.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the in vitro experimental results presented in Figure 3.

claim: CD4+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice showed a reduced capacity to differentiate into Th1 cells in vitro.
source: In addition to the effect of ceramide on CD8+ T cell function, we detected a reduced capacity of CD4+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice to differentiate into Th1 cells, but to a higher extent into Tregs in vitro (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: CD4+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice showed a higher capacity to differentiate into Tregs in vitro.
source: In addition to the effect of ceramide on CD8+ T cell function, we detected a reduced capacity of CD4+ T cells from Asm/CD4cre mice to differentiate into Th1 cells, but to a higher extent into Tregs in vitro (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C, D)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by in vitro differentiation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Synaptic ceramide signal in Ac-deficient T cells was highly elevated compared to Asm-deficient T cells.
source: Indeed, synaptic ceramide signal in Ac-deficient T cells was highly elevated compared to Asm-deficient T cells (Figure 7B), emphasizing that ceramide is involved in TCR clustering and the interaction of T cells with antigen-presenting cells (APCs).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy quantification data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Ceramide is involved in TCR clustering and the interaction of T cells with antigen-presenting cells.
source: Indeed, synaptic ceramide signal in Ac-deficient T cells was highly elevated compared to Asm-deficient T cells (Figure 7B), emphasizing that ceramide is involved in TCR clustering and the interaction of T cells with antigen-presenting cells (APCs).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the microscopy data shown in Figure 7.

claim: Elevated percentages of tumor-infiltrating Foxp3+ Tregs were detected in Asm/CD4cre mice compared to control littermates.
source: In line with results from Asm-KO mice (Figure 1B), we detected elevated percentages of tumor-infiltrating Foxp3+ Tregs as well as reduced frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in dLNs from Asm/CD4cre mice compared to control littermates (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Reduced frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in dLNs were detected in Asm/CD4cre mice compared to control littermates.
source: In line with results from Asm-KO mice (Figure 1B), we detected elevated percentages of tumor-infiltrating Foxp3+ Tregs as well as reduced frequencies of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells in dLNs from Asm/CD4cre mice compared to control littermates (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Absolute cell numbers of intratumoral T cells were reduced in Asm/CD4cre mice compared to WT littermates.
source: Moreover, absolute cell numbers of intratumoral T cells were reduced in Asm/CD4cre mice compared to WT littermates.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: TILs from T cell-specific Asm-deficient mice showed decreased expression of IFN-γ, TNF-α, and granzyme B.
source: TILs from T cell-specific Asm-deficient mice showed decreased expression of IFN-γ and TNF-α, as well as granzyme B indicating a reduced anti-tumoral T cell response (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Ceramide accumulates at the contact site between T cell and CD3/CD28 MACSiBead particle.
source: Indeed, ceramide accumulates at the contact site between T cell and particle.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: Co-localization of TCR and ceramide suggests an involvement of ceramide in TCR signaling.
source: This co-localization of TCR and ceramide suggests an involvement ceramide in TCR signaling.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the microscopy data shown in Figure 5.

claim: T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice are deficient for Ac.
source: To further validate the important role of ceramide in CD8+ T cell responses, we made use of Asah1fl/fl/Cd4cre/+ Ac/CD4cre mice. In these mice, T cells are deficient for Ac, the enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of ceramide into sphingosine.
evidence: This is stated in the results and describes the genetic model used.

claim: Both CD8+ and CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice lack Ac expression.
source: As validated by qPCR, both CD8+ and CD4+ T cells lack Ac expression (Figure 6A, Figure 6—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice have elevated ceramide concentrations compared to control WT littermates.
source: resulting in elevated ceramide concentrations in unstimulated and anti-CD3/anti-CD28 T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice compared to control WT littermates (Asah1fl/fl/Cd4+/+) (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: CD8+ and CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice showed significantly elevated phosphorylation of ZAP70 and PLCγ compared to control CD8+ T cells.
source: Indeed, CD8+ and CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice showed significantly elevated phosphorylation of the TCR signaling molecules ZAP70 and PLCγ compared to control CD8+ T cells (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The elevated phosphorylation of ZAP70 in Ac-deficient CD8+ T cells was confirmed by western blot analysis.
source: The elevated phosphorylation of ZAP70 was further confirmed by western blot analysis of isolated Ac-deficient CD8+ T cells (Figure 6D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by western blot data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Stimulation of CD8+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice led to an increased expression of granzyme B compared to CD8+ T cells from control littermates.
source: Well in line with these data, stimulation of CD8+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice led to an increased expression of granzyme B compared to CD8+ T cells from control littermates (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: CTLs from Ac/CD4cre/OT-I mice showed an improved killing capacity in comparison to control cells.
source: Strikingly, CTLs from Ac/CD4cre/OT-I mice showed an improved killing capacity in comparison to control cells (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by killing assay data shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Ac ablation had no impact on Th1 differentiation in regard to IFN-γ expression.
source: Although Ac ablation had no impact on Th1 differentiation in regard to IFN-γ expression, CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice showed an enhanced expression of granzyme B under Th1-polarizing conditions in vitro (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice showed an enhanced expression of granzyme B under Th1-polarizing conditions in vitro.
source: Although Ac ablation had no impact on Th1 differentiation in regard to IFN-γ expression, CD4+ T cells from Ac/CD4cre mice showed an enhanced expression of granzyme B under Th1-polarizing conditions in vitro (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ablation of Asm resulted in lower cellular and synaptic ceramide levels associated with impaired CD8+ T cell function.
source: However, ablation of Asm resulted in lower cellular and synaptic ceramide levels associated with impaired CD8+ T cell function, suggesting that other sphingomyelinases are not able to fully compensate for Asm deficiency in T cells.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental results presented throughout the study.

claim: Ac/CD4cre mice showed a significant reduction in tumor size compared to control mice.
source: In contrast to Asm/CD4cre mice, Ac/CD4cre mice showed a significant reduction in tumor size compared to control mice (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by tumor growth data shown in Figure 8A.

claim: Ac/CD4cre tumor-bearing mice showed elevated T cell activation reflected by increased IFN-γ and granzyme B expression of CD4+ and CD8+ TILs compared to control mice.
source: This was reflected by increased IFN-γ and granzyme B expression of CD4+ and CD8+ TILs in comparison to control mice (Figure 8C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 8C.

claim: Enhancing cell-intrinsic ceramide by ablation of Ac activity promotes T cell function.
source: From these results, we conclude that enhancing cell-intrinsic ceramide by ablation of Ac activity promotes the T cell function, whereas reduced ceramide levels due to loss of Asm activity are accompanied by a decrease in the activity of T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented in Figures 4 and 8.

claim: Reduced ceramide levels due to loss of Asm activity are accompanied by a decrease in the activity of T cells.
source: From these results, we conclude that enhancing cell-intrinsic ceramide by ablation of Ac activity promotes the T cell function, whereas reduced ceramide levels due to loss of Asm activity are accompanied by a decrease in the activity of T cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental results presented in Figures 4 and 8.
